title: Regular generation of nested ideals with a flat quotient
statement: Let $u:(R,\mathfrak m_R)\to(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ be a flat local homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of Noetherian local commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means $u(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$. Assume $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$ and $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$ be ideals with $IS\subseteq J$, and assume that the induced local ring map $R/I\to S/J$ is flat. Then $J$ is generated by a finite $S$-regular sequence if and only if $I$ is generated by a finite $R$-regular sequence and $J/IS$ is generated by a finite $(S/IS)$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Each generating sequence lies in the maximal ideal of its ring; empty sequences are allowed.

source.place: Tag 09PX (lemma-perfect-map-ci), equivalence (1) and (3), specialized to S/J flat over R/I (hence Tor dimension zero).

proof.text: Put $A=R/I$, $B=S/IS$, and $M=S/J$, viewed also as a cyclic $B$-module. Since $IS\subseteq J\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, the quotient-local-structure lemma gives nonzero local rings $A,B,M$; their maximal ideals are the images of those of $R,S,S$. The surjective-image lemma gives that $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian. The map $A\to B$ is local and flat: $B\cong A\otimes_R S$, by $\bar r\otimes s\mapsto u(r)s\bmod IS$, and flat module base change applies to the flat $R$-module $S$. Its closed fibre is $B/(\mathfrak m_R/I)B\cong S/\mathfrak m_RS$. Also $u$ is faithfully flat by the flat-local-homomorphism lemma. These identifications all use the specified quotient maps.

source.place: Tag 09PX (lemma-perfect-map-ci), quotient setup in both implications

proof.text: First suppose $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is generated by an $R$-regular sequence and $J/IS$ by a $B$-regular sequence $\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_t$. Lift each $\bar g_j$ to $g_j\in J$. Faithfully-flat ascent makes $u(f_1),\ldots,u(f_r)$ regular in $S$. The concatenation $u(f_1),\ldots,u(f_r),g_1,\ldots,g_t$ generates $J$: subtract lifts of the expression of any class in $J/IS$ in the $\bar g_j$, and the remainder is in $IS=(u(f_i))$. It is regular by the definition: the first successive quotients are those of the image sequence and the later ones are $B/(\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_{j-1})$; its final quotient is the nonzero ring $S/J$. This also proves the assertion when either list is empty.

source.place: Tag 00LM (lemma-flat-increases-depth) and lemma-join-regular-sequences; dpa.tex Tag 09PX, (3) to (1)

proof.text: For the converse assume $J$ is generated by a regular sequence. Regard $K=M[0]$ as an object of $D(B)$. It is pseudo-coherent by the Noetherian cohomology criterion: its only nonzero cohomology is the cyclic, hence finitely generated, $B$-module $M$ in degree zero. As an $A$-module, $M$ is flat by the hypothesis on $R/I\to S/J$. Apply the bounded-flat-complex Tor-amplitude lemma to the complex $M[0]$ over $A$, with $a=b=0$. Thus $H^i(M[0]\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}k_A)=0$ for $i\ne0$, where $k_A=R/\mathfrak m_R$.

Apply the regular-fibre local perfectness criterion to $A\to B$, $K=M[0]$, and $[a,b]=[0,0]$. Step 1 gives a flat local map with regular closed fibre, and Step 3 supplies pseudo-coherence and the residue-tensor bound. If the regular closed fibre has dimension $d$, this gives $H^j(M[0]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N[0])=0$ outside $[-d,0]$ for every $B$-module $N$. The derived-module Tor comparison identifies its degree $-i$ cohomology with $\operatorname{Tor}^B_i(M,N)$ for $i\ge0$. Hence $M$ has finite Tor dimension over $B$.

source.place: Tag 09PC (lemma-perfect-over-regular-local-ring), applied as in dpa.tex Tag 09PX, (2) to (3)

proof.text: Apply the single-ring nested-ideal lemma to the Noetherian local ring $S$, the ideals $IS\subseteq J\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, and the quotient $S/J$. Its regular-generation hypothesis on $J$ is the present assumption, and its finite-Tor-dimension hypothesis over $S/IS=B$ is Step 4. It follows that $IS$ is generated by an $S$-regular sequence and $J/IS$ is generated by a $B$-regular sequence. It remains to descend regular generation of $IS$ to $I$.

source.place: Tag 09PW (lemma-regular-sequence), used in the proof of Tag 09PX

proof.text: Choose a basis of $I/\mathfrak m_RI$ over $k_R=R/\mathfrak m_R$ and lifts $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in I$. The residue-extension minimal-generators lemma says that the lifts generate $I$, including $r=0$. Flatness makes the multiplication map $I\otimes_R S\to S$, $a\otimes s\mapsto u(a)s$, injective; its image is $IS$, so it identifies $I\otimes_R S$ with $IS$. Tensor right exactness, applied to reduction modulo $\mathfrak m_S$, now gives the canonical identification $IS/\mathfrak m_SIS\cong I\otimes_R k_S\cong(I/\mathfrak m_RI)\otimes_{k_R}k_S$, carrying $u(f_i)$ to $\bar f_i\otimes1$. Here $k_S=S/\mathfrak m_S$ and locality induces the field map $k_R\to k_S$. The same residue-extension lemma says these classes form a $k_S$-basis.

source.place: Tag 09PX, final paragraph: a minimal system of generators of I stays minimal for IS under a flat local map

proof.text: Use the generator-lifting lemma with both of its local rings equal to $S$, its homomorphism the identity, and its ideal $IS$. The identity induces the identity on residue fields and on $IS/\mathfrak m_SIS$, as required by that lemma. Step 5 supplies a regular generating list of $IS$, and Step 6 supplies the residue-space basis with lifts $u(f_1),\ldots,u(f_r)$. The lemma therefore proves that this particular list is an $S$-regular sequence. This identity-map specialization does not assume that $R\to S$ induces an isomorphism of residue fields.

source.place: Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators) and Tag 09CC (lemma-noetherian-finite-all-equivalent), as used in dpa.tex Tag 09PX, final paragraph

proof.text: For each $i$, put $Q_i=R/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$. Tensor right exactness identifies $Q_i\otimes_R S$ with $S/(u(f_1),\ldots,u(f_{i-1}))$, with $q\otimes s\mapsto u(q)s$ interpreted on representatives. Multiplication by $f_i$ tensors to multiplication by $u(f_i)$ and is injective there by Step 7. Faithfully-flat reflection of exactness, applied to $0\to Q_i\xrightarrow{f_i}Q_i$, makes multiplication by $f_i$ injective on $Q_i$. The final quotient is $R/I\ne0$ by Step 1. Thus the definition of regular sequence gives that $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ is an $R$-regular sequence generating $I$. For $r=0$ there are no multiplication conditions and the same nonzero final quotient applies. Together with Step 5 this proves the converse.
